current_formulation: CheckThat! 2020 asks annotators an objective question (does the text hold a verifiable factual claim) and a subjective question (should a fact-checker verify it); both must be yes.

steps.formulation: ClaimBuster calls a factual sentence check-worthy when the general public wants to know whether it is true.
steps.quote: These sentences contain factual claims and the general public will be interested in knowing whether the claims are true or false.

criticism.quote: The ClaimBuster system did not try to mimic the check-worthiness decisions for any specific fact-checking organization

steps.formulation: CheckThat! 2018 ranks debate sentences by how one fact-checker, FactCheck.org, selected them.
steps.quote: mimic the selection strategies of a particular fact-checking organization

criticism.quote: Due to the subjective nature of check-worthiness, we chose to represent the check-worthiness criteria by several questions

steps.formulation: Full Fact labels whether a sentence holds a checkable claim and leaves importance to fact-checkers.
steps.quote: We chose to decouple the importance of the claim from the claim itself.

criticism.quote: At the level of all the 7 granular categories the inter-annotator agreement is moderate

steps.formulation: CheckThat! 2020 splits the label into an objective verifiable-claim question and a subjective priority question.
steps.quote: we consider as worth fact-checking the tweets that received a positive answer both to Q1 and to Q5

criticism.quote: Check-worthiness and rumourousness can be subjective.
